Administrator: Welcome to the City Adult Learning Centre. Can I help you?
Student: Yes, I'd like to enrol on a language course.
Administrator: Which language are you interested in?
Student: I was thinking of Italian, but my company is opening an office in Seoul, so I'd better learn Korean.
Administrator: We have a beginners' Korean class. Can I take your name?
Student: Oliver Brennan. B-R-E-N-N-A-N.
Administrator: Thank you. Have you studied Korean before?
Student: Not really. I know how to say hello, that's all.
Administrator: Then the beginners' level is right. The class runs on Tuesday and Thursday evenings, from 6.30 to 8.
Student: Thursdays are difficult for me. Is there another option?
Administrator: There's a Saturday morning class, 10 till 1, once a week.
Student: That would suit me better. Saturday, please.
Administrator: Fine. The course lasts twelve weeks and costs 240 pounds. If you work for a company with more than fifty staff, you get a discount, so it's 195.
Student: My company is quite big, so I should get that.
Administrator: Great, but you'll need to bring a letter from your employer. You'll also need to buy the course book, which is about twenty pounds.
Student: OK. Where will the class be?
Administrator: In Room 14, on the second floor. Now, how would you like to pay?
Student: By card, please.
Administrator: Lovely. The first lesson is on the 5th of October.

passage:
Mechanic: Hi there, Spokes Bike Workshop. What can I do for you?
Customer: Hello. My bike's making a strange noise and the gears keep slipping. Could you have a look at it?
Mechanic: Sure. Let me take some details. Your name?
Customer: Ingrid Solberg. S-O-L-B-E-R-G.
Mechanic: Thanks, Ingrid. What kind of bike is it?
Customer: It's a hybrid. Silver, about five years old.
Mechanic: OK. And the main problem is the gears?
Customer: Yes, and I think the brakes are a bit weak too, the back one especially.
Mechanic: Right. I'll check both. We have two service options. The basic service is 35 pounds, which covers brakes and gears. The full service is 70 and includes cleaning everything and checking the wheels.
Customer: The bike hasn't been serviced for years, so I'll go for the full one.
Mechanic: Good idea. When can you bring it in?
Customer: Tomorrow morning? Oh, no, I've got a meeting. Could I drop it off on Thursday?
Mechanic: Thursday's fine. We open at eight.
Customer: And when will it be ready?
Mechanic: Usually the next day, so Friday afternoon.
Customer: Great. Do you need a phone number?
Mechanic: Yes, please.
Customer: It's 07523 680 194.
Mechanic: We'll text you when it's done. Also, if we need to replace the chain, it'll cost an extra fifteen pounds. Is that OK?
Customer: Yes, go ahead. Oh, and could you put a basket on the front? I've been meaning to get one.
Mechanic: No problem.

Adviser: Good morning, Northgate Insurance claims department. My name's Ravi. How can I help?
Caller: Hello. I need to report some water damage in my flat. A pipe burst in the flat above mine.
Adviser: I'm sorry to hear that. First, can I check your name?
Caller: Yes, it's Eleanor Whitfield. W-H-I-T-F-I-E-L-D.
Adviser: Thank you. When did you notice the damage?
Caller: On Sunday evening. I'd been away for the weekend, so it could have started on Saturday.
Adviser: We'll record Sunday as the date of discovery. Which rooms are affected?
Caller: Mainly the kitchen. I thought the bedroom was fine, but there's a damp patch on that ceiling too.
Adviser: I'll note kitchen and bedroom. What items have been damaged?
Caller: The worst thing is the carpet in the hallway, which is completely soaked. And a wooden table.
Adviser: Have you contacted the neighbour upstairs?
Caller: Yes, and he's spoken to his own insurer. His policy number is something I can send you.
Adviser: That would help. Now, have you arranged for anyone to dry the flat?
Caller: A plumber came on Monday to check the pipes, and he recommended a drying company. They said it would take about 10 days.
Adviser: 10 days. Are you able to stay in the flat in the meantime?
Caller: Not really. The electricity has been switched off in the kitchen. I'm staying with my brother.
Adviser: Your policy covers alternative accommodation up to 2,000 pounds, so keep receipts. An inspector will visit on Friday morning.
Caller: Friday's fine. Thank you.
